en.headline: Three arrested over flour-laced threat letters in renovation fee dispute
en.dek: Police held two principals and a staff member of a Kwun Tong renovation firm after a catering group received more than 30 letters containing white powder confirmed as flour.
body: Police arrested three people from a Kwun Tong renovation company on suspicion of criminal intimidation after a catering group received more than 30 threat letters containing white powder.

Officers took reports between 6 and 8 October from staff, security and residents near the group's outlets in Tsim Sha Tsui and Tseung Kwan O. The letters included paper printed with skulls and the words "toxic". Explosive Ordnance Disposal teams confirmed the powder contained no chemical, biological or radioactive substances and was ordinary flour.

Investigation showed the catering group and the renovation firm were in a money dispute of over HK$1 million over works at at least two outlets. On 9 October, police staked out the company's office and arrested two male principals and one female staff member aged 45 to 65. Stamps, envelopes, a photocopier and a computer were seized. The three were released on bail.
Police said further forensic examination of the letters is under way and more arrests are not ruled out.

zh.headline: 裝修公司3人涉寄麵粉恐嚇信被捕 追討百萬工程費
zh.dek: 警方拕捕觀塘裝修公司兩名負責人及一名職員，涉嫌因金錢糾紛向餐飲集團寄出逾30封載有麵粉的恐嚇信。
body: 警方拕捕一間觀塘裝修公司的兩名負責人及一名職員，涉嫌刑事恐嚇，因一個餐飲集團接獲超過30封載有白色粉末的恐嚇信。
人員於10月6日至8日接獲多宗報案，指集團尖沙咀及將軍澳分店、辦公室及附近居民收到信件，內附印有骷高圖案及「有毒」字樣的紙張。爆炸品處理組檢驗後證實粉末不含化學、生物或輻射物質，屬普通麵粉。
調查顯示，餐飲集團與裝修公司因至少兩間分店工程涉及逾100萬元金錢糾紛。10月9日，警方在公司辦公室埋伏，拕捕兩名男負責人及一名女職員，年齡介乎45至65歲，並檢獲郵票、信封、影印機及電腦。三人獲准保釋。
警方稱信件將作進一步法證檢驗，不排除有更多人被捕。
